replacement: “Karamazov had been frantically jealous of everyone. Yet before this first lover he simply collapsed, so to speak, and effaced himself on the spot. That makes it stranger still, since he seems to have given this formidable rival hardly a thought. He saw him as a danger far away, and Karamazov always lives in the present. Perhaps he took him for a fiction. But his wounded heart saw at once that the woman had been hiding this new rival from him and deceiving him. The man was anything but a fiction to her. He was the one hope of her life. The moment Karamazov grasped this, he gave in.

“Here we see, in excess, the love of effect, the romantic despair and sentimentality, and the wild recklessness of the Karamazovs. Yes, but there is something more, gentlemen of the jury, something that cries out in the soul, throbs without rest in the mind, and poisons the heart unto death. That _something_ is conscience, gentlemen of the jury, its verdict, its terrible torments! The pistol will settle everything, the pistol is the only way out! But _beyond_—I do not know whether Karamazov, at that moment, asked himself ‘What lies beyond?’ or whether a Karamazov could, like Hamlet, ask ‘What lies beyond?’ No, gentlemen of the jury, they have their Hamlets, but we still have our Karamazovs!”

“What need had he to be careful? Two or three times he came close to confessing. He hinted at it, he all but said it outright.” (Then came the witnesses’ evidence.) “He even shouted to the peasant who was driving him, ‘Do you know you are driving a murderer!’ But he could not speak out. He had to reach Mokroe and finish his romance there. And what was waiting for the luckless man? Almost from the first minute at Mokroe he saw that his unbeatable rival might not be so unbeatable after all, and that the toast to their new happiness was neither wanted nor welcome. But you know the facts, gentlemen of the jury, from the preliminary inquiry. Karamazov’s triumph over his rival was complete, and his soul entered a wholly new phase, perhaps the most terrible one it has passed through or ever will.
